method.method_draft: First describe the diagram and label the five regions: A = upper-left, B = upper-right, C = lower-left, D = lower-middle, E = lower-right. From the image, the touching pairs are A-B, A-C, A-D, B-D, B-E, C-D, and D-E. Then count colorings by a convenient order. Choose D first: 5 choices. Choose A next: it must differ from D, so 4 choices. Choose B: it must differ from both A and D, so 3 choices. Choose C: it must differ from A and D, so 3 choices. Choose E: it must differ from B and D, so 3 choices. Multiply to get 5·4·3·3·3 = 540.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram and convert it to a graph with vertices A = upper-left, B = upper-right, C = lower-left, D = lower-middle, E = lower-right. The image shows that A, B, and D form a triangle of mutually touching regions. Also, C touches exactly A and D among that triangle, and E touches exactly B and D. Thus the graph is a base triangle A-B-D with two extra vertices attached to already-colored edges A-D and B-D. For q colors, the triangle can be colored in q(q-1)(q-2) ways.
